original_driver.existing_behavior: Runs five first checks, then sorted root verify_*.py except explicitly optional verify_local_checkpoint_059.py, then native-evidence/*/verify.py.

proposed_steps: Place the successor bundle in a dedicated subdirectory outside the root verify_*.py glob, with its pinned helper and CROSSWALK-059.json. Keep the old 15 scripts, historical manifests and direct-link records unchanged.

Create a separately named successor driver based on the captured driver. Preserve the original five first checks, existing optional exclusion, sorted verifier order and native checks. In the existing sorted remaining sequence only, dispatch the 15 mapped names to their corresponding successors with --publication set to the publication tree and no --baseline-dir when the reconstructed files occupy baseline-059/. All other checks retain their exact original commands.

Before dispatch, verify the bundle manifest and pinned crosswalk. Reject symlinks in evidence and reconstruction trees; do not use symlink overlay or copy the whole publication. The successor reads and validates the two public blobs separately and binds original tuples to the unchanged transport manifest.

For each substituted check, record status qualified_original_to_public_crosswalk and capture its source-script and successor hashes. Do not report an old exact-byte verifier as passed or claim the original and public blobs match. Preserve strict identity for all non-059 inputs.

Record the seven analyzed semantic references and require additional review of dynamic or external consumers and other path fields. The path strings become markers; do not claim they remain usable filesystem locations.

Run the full successor driver only as a separate evidence-verification action after integration. Its result must separately state any failure and all outstanding evidence gaps; the 15 staged checks here are not proof the full driver passes or that any product behavior was validated.

open_issues: The current root driver still auto-runs the 15 old exact-byte scripts; simply adding successor scripts does not integrate them.
Other semantic consumers and direct or indirect references outside the scoped inventory may need attention; only the seven captured overlap references were compared here.
The original/private transformation was verified in the previous local recovery packet; the public-only successor checks cannot reconstruct or inspect private paths.
Historical Git objects and earlier exports can still contain private paths; this plan does not modify or purge Git history.
Symlink rejection is a preflight over the evidence and public directories, not an atomic guarantee against concurrent filesystem races.
